text:
maria_ops: Heads-up — planning a short maintenance 'lane' tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC across az6/az7 to apply NIC microcode + reboot a subset of GPU hosts. Keeping it rolling, not a full pool drain.
kevin_sre: Ping — what's our target capacity delta? how many GPUs will we lose concurrently? :thinking_face:
jana_oncall: We should cap concurrent down to 6% of regional GPU capacity. Anything more and tail latencies spike for burst tenants.
maria_ops: Planning cohorts of 10 hosts per 30m window, expected ~120 GPUs offline at any single cohort, ~3.5% steady. We can increase to 15/30m if backfill is healthy.
tim_infra: We'll cordon with this sequence: ```kubectl label node <node> maintenance=true && kubectl cordon <node> && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` then trigger vm reboot play. I'll paste exact commands in runbook.
kevin_sre: Make sure autoscaler target tracking is temporarily relaxed so it doesn't overprovision and blow cost. We'll flip scale policy to allow warm backfill only, not aggressive spin-up.
maria_ops: Good call. Ops-bot: scheduled window created in calendar; rolling groups: cohort-A (az6 east racks 3–5), cohort-B (az7 west racks 1–4), fallback cohort-C for spillover.
jana_oncall: @kevin_sre can you run a quick dry-run tonight during quiet window — simulate cordon on 1 host and verify kv-cache reseed time and prefix-cache warmup? We don't want cache-miss storm.
kevin_sre: Will do. I'll run `kvtool seed --nodes N` and capture p95 token latency. I'll post logs. :eyes:
maria_ops: Customer comms: product asked for a brief note to HOSTED customers confining to 02:00-04:00 UTC, minimal impact, no API changes. Can someone draft? Keep it short.
jana_oncall: Draft: "Planned rolling maintenance in region XYZ on 02:00-04:00 UTC. Some requests may route to secondary pools with slightly higher latency; no data loss expected. If you rely on pinned dedicated capacity, contact support." Approve?
tim_infra: Approve. Add link to status page post-deploy and runbook link.
maria_ops: Cost note: if autoscaler overshoots we'll see temporary 30%-ish GPTU cost bump. We'll monitor and kill any unneeded spinners.
kevin_sre: Also watch inter-AZ egress. During cohort handoffs we've historically seen 10-12% transient egress increase due to cache repop. Set egress throttle guard at 120% baseline.
jana_oncall: I'll enable temporary netpol rate-limit and egress cap at the infra edge for the window.
maria_ops: Rollback plan: if p95 > 200ms for > 5m, or error rate > 0.5% sustained, we stop and reverse the cohort, bring nodes back, and open incident. Oncall will page.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: infra-maint/1777779998 -> cohort-A; ETA 02:10 UTC.
kevin_sre: Took a snapshot of metrics before dry-run: p50 12ms, p95 82ms, tail 210ms. We'll compare after test.
tim_infra: Note: some legacy rack BMCs take longer to come up — add 10m buffer for rack-3 nodes.
maria_ops: Confirmed. Sequence adjusted: start rack-4 then rack-3 to avoid simultaneous slow BMCs.
jana_oncall: Reminder: tag all maintenance nodes in telemetry with `maintenance_lane=1777779998` so cost and incident queries can filter.
maria_ops: After window we'll run a 15m canary with 5% traffic to verify KV seeding and throughput before full traffic.\eke: (reaction) ops-bot: :white_check_mark: window scheduled, runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/maintenance-lane-1777779998
kevin_sre: I'll post dry-run results by 23:30 UTC. If anything flakey, escalate to infra lead.
maria_ops: Thanks team. I'll post final customer note and update status page 30m before start.
jana_oncall: Copy. Paging policy enabled.
kevin_sre: Dry-run complete — small kv reseed spike for 90s, p95 rose to 120ms; no error increase. Good to go.
maria_ops: Great. Closing planning here. Will open comms thread in #customer-success to sync message. :thumbsup:
